advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Carry `databaseId` (as e.g. `database_id`) through the `_fetch_runs` dict comprehension and use it in `main()` instead of relying on `latest.get("databaseId", 0)`.
evidence: harvest_gha.py:54: `"conclusion,createdAt,headSha,databaseId",` — databaseId is requested from gh
harvest_gha.py:61-68: dict comprehension maps only `conclusion`, `created_at`, `head_sha` — `databaseId` is dropped
harvest_gha.py:101: `log = _fetch_coverage_log(args.repo, latest.get("databaseId", 0))` — key absent, always defaults to 0
ABSENCE: no test exercises `_fetch_runs`/`main`, so the broken coverage path is not caught by CI
advisory.finding: `_fetch_runs` requests `databaseId` from `gh` but its dict comprehension never maps it into the returned run dicts, so `main()`'s `latest.get("databaseId", 0)` always resolves to 0 and `_fetch_coverage_log` always fetches run id 0 — coverage harvesting is silently broken.
scenarios: Running the harvester against a real repo: it always calls `gh run view 0 --log`, which errors or yields no coverage.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `"database_id": r.get("databaseId")` to the comprehension and change main() to `latest.get("database_id")` with a None guard before calling `_fetch_coverage_log`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Relax the coverage regex to match a `TOTAL` line embedded after gh --log line prefixes (drop the `^` anchor or match `(?m)^.*\bTOTAL\b`), and add a fixture reflecting real gh --log formatting.
evidence: github_actions.py:22-24: `re.compile(r"^TOTAL\b.*?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)%", re.MULTILINE)` — anchored to line start
harvest_gha.py:76: `["gh", "run", "view", str(run_id), "--repo", repo, "--log"]` — gh --log prepends job/step/timestamp columns per line
test_gha_adapter.py:31: fixture uses bare `TOTAL ... 84.2%` with no gh prefix, so the test passes while the production path fails
advisory.finding: `_TOTAL_COVERAGE_RE` anchors on `^TOTAL` (MULTILINE), but coverage logs are fetched via `gh run view --log`, which prefixes every line with tab-separated job/step/timestamp columns, so `TOTAL` is never at line start and the regex won't match real gh log output.
scenarios: Parsing an actual `gh run view --log` capture: no match, coverage returns None despite a TOTAL line being present.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `re.compile(r"\bTOTAL\b.*?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)%")` (no `^`/MULTILINE) or explicitly strip gh's leading columns before parsing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `parse_coverage` test on log text with no TOTAL line asserting it returns `None`.
evidence: Source documents and implements the branch: github_actions.py:35-36 `match = _TOTAL_COVERAGE_RE.search(log_text)` / `if match is None: return None`
Docstring: 'Returns ``None`` when the log contains no ``TOTAL`` coverage line.'

Only `test_parse_coverage_from_total_line` exists (test_gha_adapter.py:22) and it asserts the match case (== 84.2); no test passes log text lacking a TOTAL line to assert `None`. ABSENCE: no `assert parse_coverage(...) is None` anywhere in the two test files.
advisory.finding: The documented `parse_coverage` -> None branch (no TOTAL line in the log) is never exercised; a regression that made the regex over-match would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `def test_parse_coverage_no_total_line(): assert parse_coverage("some pytest output\nno total here") is None`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `red_to_green_recovery` test with failure(t0)->failure(t1)->success(t2) asserting the delta equals t2 - t0 (first failure), not t2 - t1.
evidence: Docstring: 'the first ``failure`` run followed (at any later index) by a ``success`` run yields the ``created_at`` delta between them.'
Implementation guard github_actions.py:53 `if pending_failure is None:` records only the FIRST failure's timestamp.

Existing tests each use exactly ONE failure: test_gha_adapter.py:36-38 (failure@1000, success@1600) and test_gha_adapter_heldout.py:32-35 (two failures, no success). ABSENCE: no test with failure->failure->success asserting the delta is taken from the first failure — so inverting the L53 guard (record the last failure) would still pass.
advisory.finding: The `red_to_green_recovery` contract that the interval is measured from the FIRST failure (across multiple consecutive failures) to the next success is untested; a regression measuring from the LAST failure would pass all current tests.
